The database build a run reads, and the check that it is the evidence's

Source: R/build_record.R
knw_build_record.Rd

A grade or a comparison reads four things from the database besides the FWA tables: link's persist schema, the run that built it (<schema>.log_recompute's run_uid), wet's flow load (the table comment, knw_discharge_load()) and the walk installed from this package (knw_walk_md5()); fresh's version decides the comparison's regeneration. 0320 and 0330 read this record at connect and refuse a schema whose run is not the evidence ledger's, before any work, so the same command runs on any machine whose database holds the build and stops on one that does not (#87). A provincial run in link renames fresh_default and builds a new one in its place (link#361), which is the case the check catches.

Usage

knw_build_record(conn, schema, run_uid = NULL)

Arguments

conn

a DBI connection.

schema

character(1) link's persist schema.

run_uid

character(1) or NULL: the run the evidence was built on (the ledger's link_run_uid). Given, a schema built by another run, or by several, is refused.

Value

A list: schema, run_uid (the schema's runs, ;-joined), discharge_load, walk_md5, fresh_version, tokens (link's output vocabulary, c(cut =, acc =, grad =, flow =), read from the build's rows of <schema>.log, where link writes them; each NA where that log predates link 0.70.0 and carries none), log_run_uid (the runs whose log rows were read, ;-joined), log (which rows those are, as a clause a reader of log appends) and line, the record as one line for a log. A schema whose log holds two values on one axis, or rows with a token beside rows without one, is refused: it is not one build. The tokens are read over the log rows of the runs log_recompute names, because a provincial run leaves the previous run's log rows in place (#145), and over every log row where none of those runs is in log, because a build's log and its recompute's log_recompute can carry different run ids (link's four-group proofs), where it must hold one run. A run set aside that was logged after the build began is refused. The line names any run whose rows were set aside, and, where every row was read, the log run the tokens came from.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
conn <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres())
knw_build_record(conn, "fresh_default_20261017", run_uid = "20261017_004619-3f4c713b")$line
} # }
